questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Choosing a culture that I dont know much about. For me, it was also important to choose within the EU, as I could not afford going on exchange without the Erasmus grant.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very very easy! I had often heard about people having problems figuring out a new system, however, it was super easy at Helsinki University, almost as easy as at my home university, which is a system I know!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been writing the UniHelp a couple of times with different questions related to technical aspects of classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I LOVED the student helpers we had in the start, they were super sweet and helpfull throughout the stay.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me, it was super easy. I found my housing through facebook groups, however, everyone should be aware that there is a lot of scams in the facebook groups. I used common sense and did not choose anything that was "too good to be true". I investigated good areas before searching for an apartment, I found out how the normal rent was, so that I could easily see if someone posted a scam with way to low rent. I made sure to talk on the phone/facetime with my new landlord, I signed a contract and so on.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It is easy to feel left out when many of the other students live together in the Unihomes. But in my case, my group was super good to write when they were meeting up anyways. Personally, I loved living in the city, I love to have the people around and joined the local running club to find new and local friends in my area. 
I found it hard living far from everyone else, as they were all the time catching lunch together at the Viikki campus, and as I was in central, I did not often join them. But for me, it was totally worth it living in central, as I enjoyed and took advantage of living in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: What stopped me from living in the unihomes was the size of the bed, which I also discussed with many of the other students. At this age, many students do have a partner or are dating people. If you want your partner to visit you, you would want them to be easily able to stay a few nights with you, and that is simply not possible in such a small bed. Im sure that many people are also getting visits from friends, and it is just nice to be able to be able to have one sleep over in your bed.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super easy, since deadline was after arrivial this gave me the opportunity to discuss what classes to take with the other students as well as hear about the classes from the Finnish students that helped us in the start. SUPER easy process, keep it like this!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Also super easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In helsinki, I got the help from the Finnish students that helped us in the start as well as the Helsinki Univercity website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you dont get the class you want, you can write the professor and ask if there is any additional spots. I got a class this way!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was as I expected. I had hoped the classes were a bit more easy, but my expectations where that it would be challenging as I took some classes which were different from my classes at my home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The in person classes were very simillar. I have not been taking online courses at UCPH, so the online courses at Helsinki University were different from what I had experienced before.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Basic mechanisms of nervous system diseases, Scientific Programming, Human and cancer genetics, Molecular Nutrition, Systems and Cognitive Neuroscience, Basics of Clinical Trial Research

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved the Scientific Programming course! Even though it was a part of the linguistic faculty, it was very relevant to me in science. I think it is relevant to anyone working with numeric data interesting in learning about programming and what programming can help you with. Even though AI plays a really big role in this area, I think it is very important to learn the basics of how programming can help you in science.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a person who LOVES sport, I would have liked even more oportunities for sport clubs. I also found it hard finding a place to do high level sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Athletic and social/creative activites were avaliable to my knowledge.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a few different local run clubs outisde uni, which was really interesting to me as I got to meet more Finnish people and people who were not students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go experience the beautiful Finnish country and nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy as coming from another nordic country. However, the weather was difficult to adjust to in the start.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Before coming, I was told that the Finns can be quite introverted. Since I was told this before coming, I was aware and was not suprised that this turned out to be true. However, I was pleasantly suprised that the second that I started to talk to the finnish people they were super nice, spoke perfect english and made it really easy to come here as a foreigner.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The SISU;) The Finnish people are so hardcore in the winter, it was amazing to experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Decide were you want to live: If you want a social life with the other students, try and get into the Unihomes. If you are more of a city person, try and get something in the city.
2. It is COLD in helsinki in January and February, bring your warmest clothes! And ENJOY it, it is the most beautifull and different experience. 
3. If you want to know the finnish people try and meet them outside of uni, for example thorugh run clubs

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No:)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know a new culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had an overlap between UCPH and Helsinki university in January, and to do two uni courses and to do intro while intensly studying for an exam back home was really hard. I was for sure able to do it, but it was hard.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
